The present First Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred by the appellants - NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1804/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined original claimants, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 18.04.2011 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Valsad in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.208 of 2005, which was preferred under Section 163A of the M.V. Act, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.2,49,500/- with 6% per annum interest to the claimant/s,
holding Opponents No.2 and 3 i.e. owner and insurance company of the Truck bearing registration No.MKM-2193 liable, jointly and severally.

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case, as per the claimants, are as under :
2.1

That on 05.04.2005 at about 5:45 hours, deceased - Yusufbhai Umarbhai Shaikh alias Yusuf Sayed Shaikh was driving the Ambulance bearing registration No.GJ-15-K-1305 and was going on the road near Bye-pass at Rasulpur, District : Devas, Madhya Pradesh.

entities.text: Yusufbhai Umarbhai Shaikh alias Yusuf Sayed Shaikh
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: At that time, Truck bearing registration No.MKM-2193 came in excessive speed from the opposite side and in rash and negligent manner and dashed with the ambulance.
As a result, the deceased sustained serious injuries and ultimately, the deceased succumbed to the injuries.

Therefore, the legal heirs of the deceased - widow, three children and father have filed claim petition under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1804/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined seeking compensation of Rs.4,36,156/- with cost and interest for unnatural and untimely death against the present respondents before the Tribunal.

sentences.text: 2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponents No.1 and 2 have chosen not to appear and contest the claim petition before the Tribunal.
Opponent No.3 - insurance company has filed its written statement / objections by disputing all the averments made by the claimants in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.
2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal is preferred by the claimant/s for enhancement.

sentences.text: Learned advocate Mr.Amit N. Patel for the appellant/s - claimant/s has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not properly calculating the amount of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1804/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined compensation.
He has submitted that amount of award is on lower side.
He has submitted that the claim petition was filed by the claimants under Section 163A of the Act.
He has submitted that the deceased was aged about 41 years at the time of accident and was a driver.
He has submitted that at the time of accident, the monthly income of the deceased was Rs.3,300/-, which is not properly considered by the Tribunal.
He has submitted that the claimants are entitled to get compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- net, which should be awarded to the claimants.

He has submitted that the Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,49,500/-,
therefore, the claimants may be awarded with enhancement of Rs.2,50,500/- accordingly.
He has submitted that the compensation is required to be enhanced by modifying the award impugned accordingly and this appeal may be allowed.
4. Per contra, Mr. Anal Shah, learned advocate for respondent - insurance company has submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper.
The Tribunal has rightly considered the income of the deceased, the age of the deceased, the dependency and future aspect of income.
He has submitted that this appeal may be dismissed and no interference be made by this Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1804/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined 5.
It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
6. I have considered the rival submissions made by the respective parties.
I have perused the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
I have also considered the documents available on record.
7. The claim petition was filed under Section 163-A of the MV Act.
The deceased was aged about 41 years at the time of accident and was a driver and his monthly income was Rs.3,300/-, which is not properly considered by the Tribunal, which would be just and proper.

sentences.text: The question which fell for consideration before the Hon'ble Apex Court is whether the amendment in Section 163A of the M.V. Act which came into effect by Official Gazette on 22.05.2018 would relate to an accident which had occurred prior to the said date.
Here the date of accident in the matter is 16.02.2017.

The view taken by the High Court was concurrent with the observation that the amendment which is brought in force is a procedural in nature which has to be given retrospective effect and would not be anything substantive so as to effect the merits of the issue.

The Hon'ble Apex Court thus found no reason to interfere with the judgment of the High Court and agreed with the view taken considering the benevolent legislation as would unnecessarily entail the benefit to be passed on to the claimants in absence of any specific bar to the same.

6. Hence, taking into consideration the fact that the amendment by way of Official Gazette on 22.05.2018 would extent the effect by way of retrospective effect to the accident NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1804/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined which had occurred in the present matter on 16.02.2017.

7. Since the amendment provides the statutory amount of Rs.5 lakhs under the provisions of Section 164 of the M.V. Act, it is to be noted that the claimants would be entitled to the amount of Rs.5 lakhs.
However, the Tribunal   Rs.4,04,500/- which is   lakhs. ..."
8. In view of above, the amount of Rs.5,00,000/- is required to be awarded.
Therefore, total compensation would be as under, which the claimant/s is/are entitled to get.

8.5 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
